text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

*A decision on the restructuring of the paper sector may be taken next week. The Economy Minister already has studies by Salomon Brothers and Chemical Bank, neither of which includes Inapa in the creation of a national 'holding'.
*Portuguese cereal producers may be hit by new proposals for the reform of the Common Agriculture Policy (CAP) of the European Union due to the method of calculation of income subsidies.

*The company Lis Sado of the group Jose Manuel Mello will reinforce its operations on the oil terminal in Setubal, south of Lisbon, with the refuelling of ships and the building of a park to store gas.
*The global cost of the metro to the Lisbon World fair Expo 98 may total 85 billion escudos, more than double the initial budget of 35 billion escudos.
*Costs of joining the single currency for the Portuguese insurance companies may be between 2.3 and 2.9 billion escudos, the director of Cap Gemini Insurance Ian Jackson said.
*According to the so-called 'Agenda 2000' the reduction of European Union aid to Portugal will be gradual and is expected to occur after the year 2003.
